blurb: Glossy black or liver English gundog nicknamed the Peter Pan of retrievers
description: The Flat-coated Retriever is a medium-large English gundog bred to retrieve on land and water, with a dense flat black or liver coat and a cheerful nature.
answer: The Flat-coated Retriever is an English gun dog developed in the mid-19th century to retrieve game on land and in water. It stands roughly 57 to 62 cm tall, weighs about 25 to 36 kg, and is often described as energetic, friendly and slow to grow up.

body: The breed originated in England in the mid-19th century and became popular as a gamekeeper's dog. Its ancestry is thought to include Newfoundlands brought to British ports, and possibly the extinct St. John's water dog, with collie-type and setter blood added for trainability and scenting ability. The first examples appeared around 1860 and the final type was set about 20 years later.

It was later eclipsed by the Golden Retriever, which was partly bred from it, and by the end of World War II so few remained that its survival was uncertain. Careful breeding from the 1960s revived it, and Flat-coats won Best in Show at Crufts in 1980, 2011 and 2022.

The head is described as being of one piece, with a minimal stop, strong jaws, a relatively long muzzle and small pendant ears. The eyes are almond-shaped and dark brown. The topline is straight, and the well-feathered tail is carried straight off the back. Colours are black (most common), liver and yellow; yellow is a disqualification in the show ring but can compete in other events.

The breed is commonly described as eager to please and full of energy. Flat-coats may bark assertively to protect their home but are unlikely to back it up with aggression. Author Paddy Petch called them the Peter Pan of the retriever breeds because they never quite grow up. Their sense of smell has seen them used as drug-detection dogs and in guide dog breeding in the UK.
Sources give little specific care guidance, but as an energetic working retriever the breed is generally expected to need plenty of daily exercise and activity.

One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 11.7 years, below the 12.7-year average for purebreds. Cancer is a major concern: a 2004 UK health survey found about 50% of deaths were due to some form of cancer. Conditions reported in the breed include cutaneous histiocytomas and soft-tissue sarcomas.

faq.q: How long do Flat-coated Retrievers live?
faq.a: One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 11.7 years, somewhat below the purebred average.

faq.q: What colours do Flat-coated Retrievers come in?
faq.a: Black is most common, followed by liver; yellow also occurs but is disqualified in conformation shows.

faq.q: Is the Flat-coated Retriever recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 121 in Group 8, with Great Britain as the country of origin.
